concept_options.title: Room to Room
concept_options.hook: One home, four finished rooms — the scope reads as a whole house, not a bathroom.
concept_options.visual_approach: Nine still-led beats that walk the house in order — bath, powder room, bedroom, living room — each on a slow, single-direction Ken Burns move. Keeps v2's gold-hairline lower third for series continuity but rebalances the room mix so no single space owns more than three beats. Closes on the redesigned outro.
concept_options.target_audience: NJ homeowners researching a whole-home renovation or addition
key_points: The renovation covers primary bath, powder room, bedroom and living space
The finished rooms are styled and move-in ready
WA Construct has 23+ years, 2026 SAM Awards and 4x Best of Houzz
concept_options.core_message: WA Construct renovates whole homes, not single rooms.
grounded_in: landscape.saturated_angles: 5 of 7 v2 beats are the primary bathroom
brand rule: no standalone bathroom marketing
concept_options.why_this_works: The single largest defect in v2 is that a whole-home renovation reads as a bathroom remodel — five of seven photo beats are the same room, which also cuts against WA Construct's rule of never marketing standalone bathroom work. Rebalancing the shot list is the cheapest, highest-leverage fix available, and every frame needed already exists in the Drive folder.

concept_options.title: Before the Finish
concept_options.hook: Start in the unfinished rooms, end in the styled ones — the transformation is the story.
concept_options.visual_approach: Opens on the raw/empty rooms (coral bedroom, bare hallway, empty living room) held slightly longer and graded a touch cooler, then turns at the midpoint into the finished, styled spaces with warmer grade and tighter cuts. The lower third escalates: sparse early, fuller at the turn.
concept_options.target_audience: Homeowners who want proof a builder finishes what it starts
key_points: The same house is shown unfinished and then finished
The finish level rises visibly across the runtime
WA Construct carries a project from bare rooms to styled spaces
concept_options.core_message: They take a house apart and put it back together better.
grounded_in: landscape.existing_content: v2 has no escalation, beat seven is typeset like beat one
concept_options.why_this_works: v2 has no arc — seven interchangeable beats in a row. A before/after turn gives the edit somewhere to go and makes the music's build land on something. The risk is honest: the folder's unfinished frames are empty rooms rather than true construction shots, so the 'before' half is less dramatic than a real demo-to-done reel would be.

concept_options.title: Material Study
concept_options.hook: Hold on the surfaces — the marble, the brass, the joinery — and let the craft speak.
concept_options.visual_approach: Detail-led. Leans on the tight frames (gold faucet macro, shower fixtures, countertop edge, vanity light) intercut with two or three wide establishing shots. Longer holds, slower moves, minimal type.
concept_options.target_audience: Design-led buyers and architects/designers scouting a builder
key_points: Finish carpentry and fixture selection are deliberate
WA Construct is a design-build firm, not a general trades contractor
concept_options.core_message: The detail level is the proof.
grounded_in: landscape.underserved_gaps: landscape finished-primary-bathroom set is a better 16:9 fit
visual_references: countertop and shower detail frames
concept_options.why_this_works: The strongest photography in the set is the detail work. But this concept fights the brief: the detail frames are overwhelmingly bathroom, so it would deepen exactly the room imbalance the client's revision is meant to fix. Listed for completeness, not recommended.

selected_concept.rationale: Recommended, pending your approval. c1 is the only option that fixes the defect you actually raised (the living-room frame) while also correcting the room imbalance that makes a whole-home renovation read as a bathroom remodel — which is a brand rule, not a taste call. c2 is the more interesting film but its 'before' half is empty rooms rather than real construction, so it promises more than the footage delivers. c3 is beautiful and wrong for this brief: it would make the piece even more bathroom-heavy.

stages.approach: Write the nine-beat title-card map: headline copy per beat, hold durations, and the outro copy block. No narration — the piece stays music-only as in v2.

tools.role: Verify chosen stills crop cleanly to 16:9 and check safe-area for the lower third

stages.approach: Lock the shot list to specific PNG filenames, assign each a Ken Burns direction and scale so consecutive beats never move the same way, and set the crop window for each so nothing important sits under the lower third.

tools.role: Match the finished-* set to the east_brunswick set so the grade holds across the cut
Reuse and re-time the approved v2 music bed to the new runtime

stages.approach: All 25 graded stills are already downloaded from the client's Drive folder. No image generation, no stock, no TTS. Music is the exact bed extracted from the approved v2 render, extended or trimmed to the new runtime with a clean tail fade.
Write edit_decisions: cut points, per-beat Ken Burns parameters, lower-third in/out timing, outro timing, and the audio fade map. render_runtime carried through from this proposal unchanged.

tools.role: Render the hand-authored composition to 1920x1080 H.264
Mux and level the music bed

stages.approach: Hand-authored (atelier) Remotion composition rather than the stock scene-type catalog: a bespoke KenBurnsPhoto scene, the existing lower-third redrawn as a component, and the chosen outro built as its own scene with real motion. Rendered at 1920x1080/30fps to match v2.
stages.fallback_if_unavailable: BLOCKER, not a substitution. If Remotion stops resolving, stop and escalate — do not silently drop to FFmpeg Ken Burns, which would flatten the outro motion.

quality_tradeoffs.tradeoff: Reuse the v2 music bed (free, already approved) vs source a new track
quality_tradeoffs.quality_impact: No music-generation provider is configured on this machine, so a new track would mean you sourcing one. The v2 bed is already signed off and keeps v3 recognisably the same series.

quality_tradeoffs.tradeoff: Hand-authored (atelier) Remotion composition vs the stock scene-type catalog
quality_tradeoffs.quality_impact: The stock catalog cannot produce the outro you asked for — it would give you another centred text card. Hand-authoring costs more build time but is the only way the outro redesign is real.

quality_tradeoffs.tradeoff: Landscape finished-primary-bathroom stills (1536x1024, needs 1.25x upscale) vs portrait east_brunswick stills (1632x2176, native res but hard crop)
quality_tradeoffs.recommendation: Prefer the landscape set for wides, keep two portrait frames for tight details
quality_tradeoffs.quality_impact: The 1.25x upscale is invisible at 1080p; the portrait crop was visibly tight in v2 and threw away the window light.

alternative_paths.description: HyperFrames (HTML/CSS/GSAP) instead of Remotion for the whole piece
FFmpeg-only Ken Burns concat with a static PNG outro

line_items.operation: Re-time and fade the reused v2 music bed
Grade-match the finished-* stills to the east_brunswick set

savings_options: Nothing to save — the whole run is local. No image, video, TTS or music generation provider is configured, and none is needed.

approval.user_notes: Client asked twice for the deliverable without answering the gate questions, then confirmed after delivery: location wording stays 'BRUNSWICK' (not East Brunswick), and outro direction A (dark brand card) replaces the recommended B (photo + scrim). Concept c1, render_runtime remotion, atelier composition mode and the reused v2 music bed all stand as proposed. First render shipped with outro B; re-rendered with A on confirmation.
